learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding of the main aspects of the Internet, in terms of architectures, protocols and applications.
Ability to analyze and model protocol architectures.
Ability to design services and applications.
Ability to critically discuss the specific technical literature and to apply it in the analysis and design phase.
Ability to clearly and rigorously explain the technical characteristics and properties of network architectures and applications.
Ability to independently find technical documentation (mainly standards) on network protocols and services.

syllabus_topics: Internet Architectures, Protocols, Technologies and Services
Protocol stack: Standard ISO-OSI and TCP/IP
Applications architectures: Client->Server and Peer-to-Peer Models
Domain Name System: architecture and protocols
TCP: features; packet format; connection management; flow and congestion control; TCP evolution: Tahoe, Reno, New Reno, SACK, ECN flavor
Internet QoS management: RTP, RTPC e SIP
Autonomous Systems, ISP e Border Router: RIP, OSPF, BGP protocols
teaching_methods: Practical usage of main network monitoring tools
assessment_rules: The final examination consists of a written test and an oral discussion. The written test checks the learning level and the ability to apply knowledge to practical scenarios. Grading ranges from Fail (Insufficient) for serious conceptual errors to 29-30 and Honors (Lode) for excellent and in-depth knowledge, critical thinking, and originality. Honors is awarded for work exceeding standard expectations.
bibliography: Andrew S. Tanenbaum, Nick Feamster, David J. Wetherall, “Computer Networks”, Prentice Hall, 2021, 6th edition.
